Subject: Urgent: Checkout errors and timeouts from Redwood inference (ShopSmart)

Rafael —

We started seeing a spike in checkout failures starting ~07:45 PDT. Customers report ~15-25% of requests to Redwood's inference endpoints returning 502/504 or timing out after ~6s. Latency for successful requests has also jumped from ~120ms to 900ms p50 for the last 40 minutes. This is impacting conversion on ShopSmart (we're seeing cart abandonment).

Attached: shopsmart_error_snippet.txt (sample 502 stack + request ids), shopsmart_path_trace_20260518.zip (tcp traces, traceroutes from our frontend).

What we've tried: retried requests (backoff), short-term fallback to cached embeddings for search, but the failure mode affects checkout tax-calculation flow. Please escalate — this is high business impact. Dana (VP Ops) is on standby and has asked for exec contact.

Requested: immediate triage, mitigation plan (can you confirm whether this looks like a peering/DNS/proxy issue?), and an ETA for rollback or workaround.

Thanks,
Alex
ShopSmart Platform

On Mon, May 18, 2026 at 08:28, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Alex — thanks for the quick heads-up and the attachments. Looping in Marissa (SE), Vivek (Ops), and Grace (CS lead) for immediate triage and exec coordination.

Alex / Rafael — quick triage summary (first-pass):

Observations:
- Our edge logs show a sharp increase in latency and 502s originating from a subset of IPs that map to ShopSmart's primary peering CIDR (ip-block 203.0.113.0/24) between 07:44–08:20 PDT.
- Traceroutes indicate asymmetric return paths: several hops drop or reroute traffic to a different peering point ~3 hops before our inference fleet.
- DNS: multiple NXDOMAIN spikes and TTL refreshes from ShopSmart resolvers around the same window (likely exacerbating connection reestablishments).
- Inline proxy/WAF: 502/503 spikes correspond to a surge in concurrent connections that caused our proxy pool to start returning 502s when backend calls timed out. We also see a handful of ACL deny responses that look misclassified — suspect policy rollout on an in-path proxy.

Immediate mitigations (what I will do now):
1) Open temporary bypass route for ShopSmart CIDR — route to fallback peering (us-west-2-b-peering) to avoid the flaky transit hop (takes ~6–10m to propagate).
2) Increase proxy backend timeout to 10s for ShopSmart traffic only and increase pool size by +25% to accommodate spike.
3) Pin DNS TTL for ShopSmart-specific hostnames to 60s on our side and ask them to do the same for their resolvers.
4) Collect and attach a set of request IDs for deeper trace (attached: mitigation_steps_patch.diff showing proxy config edits).

Next ask for ShopSmart:
- Can you confirm whether you recently rolled any egress firewall or NAT changes in your VPCs?
- If you can provide pcap around 07:40–08:20 for one affected host, that would help confirm asymmetric path.

I'll push the route change now and report back in the bridge.

Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

- Notifying my director and prepping a short exec note to share with ShopSmart leadership (Dana).

Subject: Plan and timeline — ShopSmart checkout errors (follow-up)

Dana / Alex — thanks again for patience. Quick external-facing summary and plan:

Impact: ~20% of inference requests to tax/calc endpoints returned 502/504 during 07:44–08:20 PDT on 2026-05-18. Successful-request p50 latency rose from ~120ms to ~900ms during the spike.

Root cause (initial): transient peering path instability causing asymmetric routing and packet loss, compounded by DNS resolver churn from ShopSmart egress and an in-path proxy ACL/pool sizing issue on our side that amplified 502s.

Immediate mitigations completed (timeline):
- 08:42 PDT: temporary bypass route applied to route ShopSmart traffic to fallback peering (expected propagation 6–10m).
- 08:45 PDT: proxy backend timeout increased to 10s + pool scaled +25%.
- 09:02 PDT: observed error rate return to baseline for ShopSmart test traffic.

Next steps (we own / Redwood):
- Open carrier escalation and request persistent route fix (Vivek leading, ticket CLD-92021).
- Full RCA and post-mortem within 72 hours with traceroutes, packet captures, and corrective actions to prevent recurrence.
- Post-incident: we'll propose a dedicated peering/route pin for ShopSmart's critical endpoints to avoid shared transit jitter (we'll include cost/benefit).

We recognize this was high impact — Grace will coordinate customer communications and I'll keep you updated on carrier progress and the RCA. If you want a short exec call with our VP Ops (Vivek) and CTO to walk through immediate findings, we can schedule within the next 2 hours.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
